top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a discovery with a decisive experiment: the Kane-Mele Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant spin-orbit band insulators and the quantum spin Hall state, and Molenkamp's HgTe quantum-well transport observation of the quantized edge channels. Nearly two decades of independent transport, ARPES and STM work have left the interpretation stable, the physics is distinct from the 2016 topological-phase prize, and Kane, Mele and Molenkamp form a coherent trio of two joint co-originators plus the first experimentalist. The citation must stay narrow on the 2D effect to avoid implying credit for the 3D work (Hasan, Fu-Moore-Balents-Roy) or the HgTe proposers (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang), a real attribution cost. P002 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is a clean, mature invention with well-defined attribution and is a sound second choice. P000 ranks last because at least one proposal is a creditable discovery or invention.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I share an institution (Chalmers) with Goran Johansson, and have long-standing academic exchanges in Japan (Katori's country) but no documented tie to any credited laureate
